claims.text: Conventionally sintered single-phase ZrB2 requires preparation temperatures above 2300 °C.
Conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2 has relatively high porosity.
Conventionally prepared ZrB2 is susceptible to damage during exposure to a liquid plating bath.
Spark plasma sintering at approximately 2100–2150 °C can consolidate single-phase ZrB2 at a lower temperature than conventional sintering.
Optimized SPS dwell times will promote rapid consolidation and improved densification of ZrB2.
Rapid heating and short sintering durations are characteristic of SPS.
The proposed SPS treatment will increase the density of ZrB2.
The proposed SPS treatment will reduce porosity in the ZrB2 microstructure.
SPS facilitates plasma-enhanced diffusion in ZrB2.
SPS-induced diffusion and rapid densification minimize grain growth in ZrB2.
SPS-induced diffusion and rapid densification minimize pore coalescence in ZrB2.
Reduced porosity produces a more homogeneous and compact ZrB2 ceramic structure.
A more homogeneous and compact ZrB2 structure is less prone to hole formation under the thermal and chemical stresses of a liquid plating bath.
SPS-processed ZrB2 will have lower porosity than conventionally prepared ZrB2.
SPS-processed ZrB2 will have greater mechanical integrity than conventionally prepared ZrB2.
SPS-processed ZrB2 will resist damage during long-duration liquid plating exposure better than conventionally prepared ZrB2.
Higher porosity in conventionally prepared ZrB2 increases vulnerability to hole formation and mechanical failure during service.
Failure to obtain statistically significant improvements in densification, porosity, mechanical performance, or bath-exposure performance would falsify the hypothesis.
